title: Group permissions
purpose: Maintain the capabilities granted to a group of users.
summary: Choose which permissions a group grants its members.

tasks.title: Change a group's permissions
steps: Move permissions between Available permissions and Chosen permissions under [[Permissions]].

tasks.title: Grant a capability to a group's members
steps: Choose the accounts permission, such as Can view patient information or Can use emergency access, and save. A capability is never implied by a role, including admin.

good_to_know: Members are added on each user's account, not on this form.
Built-in group names are read only.
Changes are recorded in the audit history. A later save by someone else replaces yours.
Saving, here or on Add group, asks you to confirm it is you (your password, a code, or both, as the page asks), unless you confirmed in this browser in the last 5 minutes.

sections.title: Access and fields
paragraphs: The administration site requires an active account with Staff status. User and group pages additionally require Superuser status; a laboratory admin role alone or individual model permissions do not open them. These technical flags do not themselves confer operational roles or capabilities.

items.label: Name
items.description: Required unique name, at most 150 characters. On existing built-in laboratory groups the name is read only; other existing group names remain editable.

items.label: Permissions
items.description: Optional Available permissions and Chosen permissions with filtering, choose/remove and Choose all/Remove all. The accounts permission Can view patient information is the capability that lets active internal members see patient information; no role grants it by itself. The other capabilities are Can review access and audit records and Can use emergency access. Permissions do not create laboratory roles for arbitrary group names. Removing a permission waits for any change the group's members are saving at that moment, one member at a time: a member it has not reached yet can still save a change before it, and nothing they save after it has the removed capability. Adding a permission waits for nothing.

sections.title: Membership and history
paragraphs: No user/member selector is on this group form; edit membership on each User. Saves record before/after group snapshots in attributed audit events. There is no original-version token on this form, so a later valid save can replace concurrent edits. Delete is disabled.

sections.title: Confirm it is you
paragraphs: Every save of a group, new or existing, asks you, the person signed in, to confirm it is you, unless you already confirmed in this browser in the last 5 minutes. The Confirm it is you section then appears before the buttons, and nothing is saved until what you type there is accepted. Signing in does not count: only confirming again does, and a new sign-in, even in the same browser, starts without one. Once you have confirmed, no page that asks (account administration, and the session limits and second sign-in factor rule on Security settings) asks again in this browser for 5 minutes. A page opened while you were confirmed and saved after the 5 minutes passed asks then.

Confirming on Confirm your password, or with a code before a change to your own two-factor settings, counts too, once every factor your account has was given there within the last 5 minutes: each counts for 5 minutes from when it was given, so the earlier one runs out first. A confirmation here counts for those pages as well. A new password, or a new or different authenticator app, on your account since you confirmed makes the next save ask again, for both. An account with neither a password nor an authenticator app cannot confirm, so it cannot save here until it sets a password.

When the confirmation is missing or not accepted, nothing is saved, and no audit event or administration history entry is written; the name and permissions you chose stay on the page. A confirmation accepted while another field is refused is kept: the page shows that field's error without the section, and saving again within the 5 minutes does not ask.

A password or code not accepted is listed in your own Sign-in history as Re-authentication failed and counts toward the failed sign-in limit; an attempt that limit refuses is listed as Too many failed attempts. What you type in these fields is never stored, logged or put in an audit event, and the administration history does not list it among the changed fields.

items.label: Your password
items.description: Shown when your account has a password: your own current password. The help under it says what saving asks for and that you are not asked again in this browser for 5 minutes. Left empty: Enter your password to save this change. Not accepted: Incorrect password. Accepted, but the code is not: Enter your password again with the code (the page does not keep it).

items.label: Authenticator or recovery code
items.description: Shown when your account has an authenticator app: a code from it, or one of your unused recovery codes, which is then used up. Left empty: Enter a code from your authenticator app, or a recovery code, to save this change. Not accepted: Incorrect code. The password is checked first; when it is not accepted, the code is not checked and can still be used.

items.label: Too many failed login attempts. Try again later.
items.description: The failed sign-in limit refused your password or code before checking it, after too many that were not accepted. Wait a few minutes, then try again.

items.label: Too many attempts to confirm it is you. Wait a minute, then try again.
items.description: Shown after 10 tries within a minute by your account (the Confirm your password pages count too). Nothing was checked, and the refusal is not listed in Sign-in history.

items.label: Your account has no password to confirm it is you, so this change cannot be saved. Set a password on Change password first.
items.description: Your account has neither a password nor an authenticator app, so it has nothing to confirm with. Set a password from Change password in the account menu, then save again.

items.label: Your sign-in factors changed, or your confirmation ran out, while this page was open. Confirm it is you again.
items.description: An authenticator app was added to or removed from your account, or your confirmation ran out, while your save was being checked. Nothing is saved. The section now asks for what your account has: fill it in and save again.

items.label: Save
items.description: Asks you to confirm it is you first, unless you did in this browser in the last 5 minutes (see Confirm it is you); so do Save and continue editing and Save and add another. Validates and saves, then returns to the model list with preserved filters, except the user-creation flow described separately.

items.label: Save and continue editing
items.description: Saves and reopens this record’s change form.

items.label: Save and add another
items.description: Appears only when creation is permitted; saves and opens a fresh add form.

items.label: History
items.description: Existing records only: opens Django administration history, separate from attributed domain audit records.

items.label: Home / app / model breadcrumbs
items.description: Return to administration home, the application module or the current model list.

items.label: View site
items.description: Header link to the operational application. Log out submits immediate sign-out; it has no administration confirmation page.
